text:
NOTICE TO TENANTS

The building management will replace the main water supply pipes on the second and third floors between 3 and 7 March. [1] The latter option, which involves a short interruption on each floor in turn, was chosen because it keeps the rest of the building fully operational.

Water will be suspended on each floor between 9 a.m. and 1 p.m. on the day of the work, and tenants are asked to [2] any items stored beneath sinks so that the contractors can gain access. [3] the work extend beyond 7 March, the management has arranged a temporary supply from the ground-floor kitchen. Any damage caused by the contractors will be repaired at no cost to tenants, [4] it is reported to the office within seven days.

choices: Two schedules were considered: replacing all of the pipes simultaneously, or proceeding floor by floor.
Two schedules were considered, although neither could be confirmed before the contractor's report arrived.
Simultaneous replacement was ruled out after several tenants raised concerns about the noise.
The pipes were inspected last month, and those on the second floor showed signs of corrosion.
questions.explanation: 'The latter option' needs a pair of alternatives, and the one chosen is the work done floor by floor in turn; only the first sentence offers that pair.
Tenants must 'clear' (empty) the space beneath their sinks so contractors can reach the pipes; the others do not collocate with items.
'Should the work extend' is an inverted conditional that matches the base form 'extend' and the arrangement already made; 'Had' would need a past form and 'Unless' reverses the logic.
'Provided that it is reported' means on condition that; the other forms are not valid conjunctions here.

text:
Retail analysts expect consumer spending to remain subdued through the first half of next year. [1] The former is expected to ease gradually as supply chains recover, whereas the latter is likely to persist until central banks begin to reduce interest rates.

Retailers are therefore expected to [2] a cautious approach to stocking and promotions. Large chains are likely to cope reasonably well, [3] smaller independent stores will struggle to absorb higher costs without raising prices. Analysts advise investors not to [4] too much significance to a single quarter's figures, since seasonal patterns can distort short-term trends and mask the underlying direction of demand.

choices: Two factors are widely cited: persistent inflation in household services and the rising cost of borrowing.
Two forecasts were published last week: one by the central bank and one by an independent institute.
Consumer confidence fell sharply in October, and spending on durable goods declined by a similar margin.
Persistent inflation in household services was cited, and borrowing was seen as a minor concern by most analysts.
questions.explanation: 'The former' and 'the latter' require two items, and what eases as supply chains recover and what persists until rates fall are inflation and borrowing costs, so only the first sentence fits.
'Adopt a cautious approach' is the fixed collocation; 'adapt' would need 'to', and the others do not fit.
'Whereas' contrasts large chains with smaller stores; the other options do not express contrast.
'Attach significance to' is the collocation; the others cannot take 'significance to'.

text:
To: All IT staff
From: Dominika Reyes, Head of Infrastructure
Subject: Server migration update

I am writing to update you on the server migration. [1] As a result, the migration scheduled for 12 April cannot proceed as planned. Nobody had anticipated this setback. [2], the team has already identified an interim arrangement that will keep the existing systems stable until the new servers arrive.

The migration will now be [3] until the week of 3 May, and the change freeze will be extended accordingly. Staff are asked to [4] from scheduling any maintenance on the old servers during this period, as the interim arrangement leaves little margin for unplanned downtime.

choices: Unfortunately, the supplier has informed us that the delivery of the new servers will be delayed by three weeks.
Fortunately, the supplier has informed us that the new servers will be delivered three weeks ahead of schedule.
The supplier has confirmed that the new servers will be delivered on 5 April, as originally agreed.
Unfortunately, the supplier has informed us that its invoice for the new servers will be revised by three percent.
questions.explanation: 'As a result, the migration ... cannot proceed' needs a cause, and only a delay in delivery explains it.
The email moves from a setback to a solution, so a contrast ('Nevertheless') is needed; the others signal result or similarity.
'Postponed until' means moved to a later date; the others do not fit the meaning.
'Refrain from scheduling' is the standard structure; the other verbs do not take 'from' in this meaning.

text:
Dear Ms Okafor,

Thank you for submitting a proposal for the Harbour Logistics Forum. The selection committee received more than 300 submissions this year. [1] This is a considerable achievement, and we would like to congratulate you on it.

You are invited to present on 14 June in a 45-minute slot. Speakers are expected to [2] their slides by 1 June so that interpreters can prepare. We regret that we are unable to cover travel costs; [3], accommodation for two nights will be provided free of charge. If you are unable to attend, we would be [4] if you could inform us before 20 May.

Yours sincerely,
Helen Marsh
Programme Director

choices: Only forty of these were shortlisted for the main programme after a two-stage review.
Many of these were withdrawn before the review began because of changes to travel regulations.
Each of these was reviewed by at least three members of the selection committee.
The deadline for submissions was extended twice because of technical problems with the online form.
questions.explanation: 'This is a considerable achievement' and the congratulations only make sense if the proposal was among a small selected group, which the first sentence states.
Speakers 'submit' their slides; the other verbs do not take slides as an object in this sense.
The second clause offsets the first (no travel costs, but accommodation), so 'however' is needed.
'We would be grateful if you could' is the standard polite request; the others do not fit the structure.

text:
Brightwell Engineering is seeking a project coordinator for its Rotterdam office. [1] In this capacity, you will be responsible for budgets, schedules and the quality of delivery across a portfolio of infrastructure projects.

Applicants should demonstrate [2] leadership skills and at least five years' experience in a similar role. Fluency in Dutch is an advantage, and applicants will be considered on the strength of their record rather than their qualifications alone. [3] applicants hold a valid work permit, relocation support will be offered, covering travel and temporary housing for up to three months. Please submit your application by 30 June, [4] your CV and a covering letter that explains why you are suited to the role.

choices: The successful candidate will report directly to the operations director and manage a team of six.
The company was founded in 1987 and now employs more than four hundred people in three countries.
The position was created following the retirement of the previous coordinator after twelve years of loyal service to the company.
Candidates are advised to read the full application guidance carefully before submitting any of their documents.
questions.explanation: 'In this capacity' refers to a role with authority, which only the first sentence describes.
'Strong leadership skills' is the natural collocation; the others do not describe skills.
'Provided that' means on condition that; the other forms are not valid conjunctions.
'Including your CV' is a present participle introducing the required documents; the other forms are not grammatical here.
